prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create exactly ONE isolated city-map sprite for tianshu, historical Tibetan regional kit. Realistic ancient material detail and crisp restrained weathering matching the attached Song reference; reinterpret the subject in Tibetan stone/wood/cloth construction, not Chinese gray-tiled gables. Orthographic 2:1 dimetric projection, yaw45 pitch30, NO perspective convergence. BOTH ground axes MUST form exactly slopes +0.5 and -0.5 in screen space, opposite edges parallel, upright vertical posts. The ground-plane bounding diamond must be twice as wide as high. Thin natural ground contact, clearly visible LEFT, FRONT and RIGHT ground corners; no thick display slab. South/front faces screen lower left. Opaque solid object with real RGBA background transparency; no luminous rim, haze, glow, baked white or checkerboard. Warm-neutral light from screen UPPER LEFT, tiny short soft contact shadow lower right. Entire asset centered with at least10% transparent margins, no cropping. No people, animals, writing, marks resembling lettering, shop signs, watermark, labels, grid, modern elements, background scenery, road, sky, floating island, diorama base, cartoon or toy. Original generic regional adaptation; not a named historical monument. Asset ID bld_kit_tubo_stupa. A generic Tibetan chorten, small whitewashed stone Buddhist stupa on a square7m by7m ground footprint. Architectural square stepped base, smooth white bell-shaped dome, a small square harmika above the dome, tall slender tapering ringed brass spire, modest parasol and small crescent/sun finial. Restrained red-ochre molding band at base of dome, gray stone exposed at footing, no gilded entire building. A tiny pile of rounded uninscribed stones within the footprint beside the steps evokes a mani-stone boundary; no engraving or text. One short strand of plain faded red blue yellow white green fabric pennants attached to low posts entirely within footprint; no inscriptions. White plaster and solid stone material with believable restrained age, not a metal table-top votive sculpture. Keep an entirely readable square thin ground-contact outline, its left and right front edges equal length, each slope absolute0.5. Architectural stepped base belongs to stupa; no additional display pedestal. Tall sprite, preserve full finial and ample transparent margin. Regional original architectural design using bell dome and ringed spire motifs from Tibetan stupa forms, NOT a named temple reconstruction.
